commenti.body: I exclusively watched horror movies last month and this one was easily in my top 5. It's not very scary, but it's extremely smart and moving. It takes an interesting concept and executes it in an orginal and artful manner. It explores what it means to be human through an inhuman perspective. This film is basically what would have happened if Terrence Malick directed Under the Skin, so if someone likes either of those styles, they're going to love this.
One of the best movies I’ve seen in the last 3-4 years. Beautiful examination of the human condition, lovely ending.
What else was in your top 5?
The Wicker Man (my favorite), Kwiadan, Peeping Tom, Unsane and Goodnight Mommy (2014)

I definitely owe this film a rewatch. I liked that it subverts the idea that some describe The Witch as endorsing - that is, the idea of witchcraft as women’s liberation - and suggests that it’s a lot more complicated than that, not just due to the suffering inflicted upon others, but also in that the circumstances in which one might become a witch, as shown here, may be entirely out of someone’s control and thus robs one’s ability to have a good life on their own terms.

It’s also fascinating to see how different cultures have different lore about witches.
